summary:
Bermuda is a British Overseas Territory. Local legislation governs, and the United Kingdom's Equality Act 2010 and its 2025 single-sex services code do not automatically extend to Bermuda; United Kingdom measures could be applied only by Order in Council.

The House of Assembly voted 22–16 on 14 May 1994 to decriminalise consensual sex between adult men, striking two sections of the Criminal Code. The debate divided the island, with religious leaders split and the Christian Coalition staging marches against the change.

In July 2013 the Senate passed the Human Rights Amendment Act, which outlawed discrimination on grounds of sexual orientation and, in the same instrument, on grounds of age. Same-sex marriage was not permitted at that point.

The Governor gave assent to the Domestic Partnership Act in February 2018. It replaced same-sex marriage with domestic partnerships open to both same-sex and opposite-sex couples, making Bermuda the first jurisdiction to revoke marriage equality. Recognition of a same-sex partner therefore rests on the partnership register rather than on marriage.
tangentialFactors:
Organised religious hostility toward visible same-sex couples is documented. In July churches including the African Methodist Episcopal congregation protested a gay cruise calling it incompatible with the word of God and the Christian moral fibre, an episode that indicates the reception a visible same-sex couple may meet in public rather than a legal penalty.

The 1994 decriminalisation vote split the island, with religious leaders divided among themselves and the Christian Coalition marching against the reform. That division is the social backdrop to the 2018 reversal of same-sex marriage, which was itself the first such revocation recorded for any jurisdiction.
localsOnly:
Residents are protected against discrimination on grounds of sexual orientation under the Human Rights Amendment Act passed in July 2013, which added age to the same statutory instrument. This protection is a matter of local human rights law, not of United Kingdom legislation.

Residents seeking recognised partnership status use the domestic partnership register established by the Domestic Partnership Act 2017, which is open to opposite-sex couples as well as same-sex couples. Marriage is not the route available to a same-sex couple.

The 1994 amendment removed two sections of the Criminal Code, so consensual sex between adult men is not an offence locally.
outOfScopeNotes:
Whether the 2013 anti-discrimination protection has been enforced in any reported case is not sourced here; the inventory records the statute's passage, not its application.

The inventory does not address gender recognition, legal document markers, entry or visa screening, single-sex facilities, or access to gender-related care in Bermuda, and does not state whether any hate-crime provision covers bias-motivated violence against a trans person. Those questions remain unresolved against these sources.

The precise content of the United Kingdom's 2025 single-sex services code, and whether any Order in Council has ever applied a United Kingdom measure to Bermuda, are not specified in the inventory.
